title: A chart filtered to one advisor or technician equals the filtered report
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a location (workplace) with several advisors and technicians and at least two months of invoices and clocked time.
  3. Chart tooltips show whole percentages (e.g. 117%) while the reports show two decimals: compare after rounding the report figure to a whole number.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu.
  2. On Billing Efficiency set the range pill to Last 12 Months and click View details.
  3. In the chart's Advisor filter choose one advisor (any advisor in the list).
  4. Hover the chart point for last month and write down that advisor's percentage and ELR.
  5. Click Reports > Advisor Analysis, choose the same advisor in the Advisor filter and set the Date control to Last month. Write down the Totals row Billing Efficiency and ELR.
  6. Back on the Dashboard, set Technician Efficiency to Last 12 Months, click View details, and in the Technician filter keep only two technicians (any two).
  7. Hover last month's point and write down each technician's percentage.
  8. Click Reports > Technician Efficiency, Invoiced tab, Date: Last month, and write down those two technicians' Efficiency.
  9. Repeat steps 6 to 8 on Technician Utilization, comparing with the Technician Utilization report with the same two technicians chosen in its Technician filter.
  10. On Reports > Advisor Analysis keep the same advisor chosen, set the Date control to This year, and hover last month's point on the chart above the table.
  11. On the Dashboard set Billing Efficiency to This Year with the same advisor chosen and hover last month's point.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Billing Efficiency chart filtered to one advisor shows only that advisor's line, and last month's point equals the report filtered to the same advisor for last month (percentage and ELR, after rounding).
  • The Technician Efficiency chart filtered to two technicians shows only their lines, and each one's last-month point equals the report's Efficiency for that technician.
  • The Technician Utilization chart filtered the same way matches the Technician Utilization report for those technicians.
  • The chart on the Advisor Analysis report, under the report's own advisor and date filters, shows the same last-month value as the report and as the Dashboard chart with the same advisor.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9580 (S8), story SV-9583 (S11); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R1), S8 (S8-R5), S11 (S11-R7). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 05_Billing_Hover, 06_TechEff_Hover, 07_TechUtil_Hover, 11_saa_Hover, 12_te_Hover, 13_tu_Hover (whole-number tooltips).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S8-R5: “When the user changes a chart filter, the chart reloads scoped to the selected technicians or advisor.”
  • S11-R7: “The embedded chart shows the same figures as the report it sits on.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
